_about: The /draw step guide as data. Each step: what to do, when it is done, the topics to look up before doing it, and the files it produces. Before a step, run its step command: python3 "<skill>/scripts/lookup.py" --step <id> --log "<project>/.claude/draw/<slug>" [--value key=value ...]. It prints every topic in lookup_before (a {key} template is filled from --value key=..., e.g. --value move=push-in; aliases resolve through the template's aliases and the index; {form} and {approach} default to the brief's Form: and Approach: lines) and appends to docs/lookups.log one `step` line (UTC time, step id, the filled topic ids) plus one line per topic. A question that comes up mid-step is a single-topic lookup: lookup.py <topic> --log <out>. Products are paths relative to the output folder .claude/draw/<slug>/: {slug} is that folder's name, a trailing / is a folder with at least one file, * and <name> are wildcards over the folder's own files (never <out>/scratch/ or node_modules/), and <page-name>.html is the page file named on the `Page:` line of docs/ui_brief.md (no wildcard matches it). applies_to entries are alternatives; inside one entry, & joins conditions that must all hold: all, form:<diagram|map|film|component>, approach:<diagram-system|mechanism|free-creative>, when:<condition from the brief's When: line, or detected in the artifact>. A template names the plan file and line its values come from (guidance for the builder; the check does not read it) and its aliases; none lists values that name no topic, none_topic is the chapter such a value's alias opens. Optional step keys: ordered (the step prints its topics in the listed order, the first being the one read before the rest), all_products (the step delivers every produces pattern, not just one). Products and these keys are guidance for the builder: scripts/ledger-check.py checks only docs/lookups.log against this file (every applicable step has a step record, every listed topic was printed with it, and a template step filled at least one topic); lookup.py --sync-aliases writes the templates' aliases into the index.

steps.title: Preflight the toolchain
steps.do: Every form runs a browser check (verify-page, perf-check, render, archify finalize), so every build starts here: run `node "<skill>/scripts/motion/doctor.mjs" --install` until it prints READY, save its output, and export the CHROME_PATH it reports. Every Chromium the run starts goes through scripts/motion/browser.mjs launchChromium() (seeded profile), never a bare chromium.launch() and never another browser tool.
steps.done_when: docs/preflight.txt exists and its final status line is READY; CHROME_PATH is set in the shell used for later checks.

steps.title: Choose the form
steps.do: Pick diagram, map, film or component from the user's verb and audience (not the subject); an explicit --lane or named form wins, and the user is never asked. /draw makes single pieces: a request that needs a whole page (explain X, a tutorial, several figures read together) is form component with `needs-page` on the When: line, and /ui assembles the page at the end (step assemble-page).
steps.done_when: docs/brief.md has a `Form:` line holding only the value, exactly one of diagram|map|film|component, and a `Why:` line with the one-sentence reason (ledger-check reads routing lines up to the first dash, parenthesis or colon, so prose there is ignored).

steps.title: Choose the approach
steps.do: Pick diagram system, mechanism or free creative by what carries the meaning (structure, behaviour, or feeling/story); when structure and behaviour both matter, name which part is the diagram and which the mechanism.
steps.done_when: docs/brief.md has an `Approach:` line naming one of diagram-system|mechanism|free-creative (or a split with each part named) and a `When:` line listing the conditions that hold (needs-page, seek-overlay, webgl, 3d, pipes, brand, import, track, loop, long, hand-drawn, diagram-figure, ...); both lines hold values only, comma-separated, with any reason on the `Why:` line.

steps.title: Name the size class (anatomy step 1)
steps.do: Look up /draw's override first, then the upstream size chapter, and read the upstream chapter through the override: name Figure, Hero or Epic from the idea's needs; no time estimate, no proposal of a smaller tier, no question; Hero and Epic are built directly.
steps.done_when: docs/brief.md has `Size: Figure|Hero|Epic` and the same value appears in the 尺寸 field of the status line; no estimate or size question was sent; mech-overrides was looked up before anatomy-size-classes.

steps.title: Write the brief and send the 開工狀態行
steps.do: Restate what must be obvious and to whom, separating fixed facts and real assets from picture choices. Send the one-line 開工狀態行 as soon as form, approach and delivery are decided, and keep building in the same turn. A 型別或結構 or 尺寸 field that a later step decides (the diagram type at diagram-plan, the invented object at mech-invent-object, the film structure and primary format at design-film-folder, the map type at map-author) reads 待定; the step that decides it is followed by one progress line stating the value (step progress-notes).
steps.done_when: Exactly one status line matching `^開工：形式 (diagram|map|film|component)／畫法 .+／型別或結構 .+／尺寸 .+／交付 (單件|多件|元件＋/ui 組頁)／理由 .+$` was sent; docs/brief.md lists facts, real assets with paths, and decided choices; every field sent as 待定 has its decided value in a progress line recorded in docs/progress.md; no question was put to the user unless docs/brief.md has a `Missing:` line naming a real asset or fact.

steps.title: Keep the clock and the progress notes
steps.do: Run `date` now and at the start of every later step, and keep docs/progress.md: the run's start time, then one line per step with its start time and the share of the run you expect it to take. When the step that decides a status-line field sent as 待定 (型別或結構, 尺寸) is done, send one progress line with the decided value (型別或結構：…／尺寸：…) and record it. When a step runs past twice its share, send the user one progress line (做到哪、剩什麼) and keep building: no wait, no question, no smaller scope. A gated critique row that has not improved over two consecutive rounds is written under 未做到的 with its last score and the reason, and the run moves on.
steps.done_when: docs/progress.md has the start time and a line per step performed with its start time and expected share; every status-line field sent as 待定 has the progress line that gave its value; every step that ran past twice its share has the progress line that was sent; any stalled row is recorded with its last score and reason.

steps.title: Three seeds in parallel
steps.do: Make scratch/seed-a, seed-b and seed-c, each with only a copy of docs/brief.md, and start three subagents in parallel in one message: each runs every applicable step after seed-hunt and before the pick step (seed-pick, or seed-pick-film for a film) with its step commands logged to its own seed folder, never opens a sibling seed, and ends with docs/seed_note.md. Without a subagent tool, build them one after another from the brief alone. A quick request runs one seed. No style is assigned to any seed: the spread comes from independent sampling.
steps.done_when: docs/seed_hunt.md records the seed count, how they ran (parallel subagents, sequential, or 1 for a quick request) and the pick step; every seed folder that did not fail holds docs/lookups.log with a step record for every applicable step up to the pick step, and docs/seed_note.md with the idea in one sentence and its capture paths.

steps.title: Film brief (Phase 1 step 1)
steps.do: Fill the film brief block (goal, audience, the one thing to remember, length, formats, facts, real assets, UNACCEPTABLE, deliverables).
steps.done_when: docs/brief.md contains the template's FILM, ASSETS, VISUAL, UNACCEPTABLE and DELIVER fields; every real-asset path listed exists, or the run stopped naming it.

steps.title: Client-work constraints
steps.do: Label a sample `Concept demo`, use no third-party logos or invented results, and keep copy, colours and asset paths apart from the motion so revisions stay cheap.
steps.done_when: docs/brief.md records the Concept-demo label and the separated copy/colour/asset config file; no third-party logo appears in assets/.

steps.title: Turn a pasted product URL into real assets
steps.do: Run `node "<skill>/scripts/motion/grab.mjs" <url> --out "<project>/.claude/draw/<slug>/brand"` for screenshots at the three formats and the computed fonts and colours.
steps.done_when: The grab manifest.json exists in the output folder and docs/style_guide.md cites its fonts and colours.

steps.title: Style guide, ban list, identity locks, motion tokens
steps.do: Read the supplied reference into decided lines (or take the restrained typographic direction when none was supplied, without asking), write the ban list and identity locks in numbers, and set the motion tokens. For a free-creative component this is the component's own look.
steps.done_when: docs/style_guide.md has the decided look lines with Keep/Leave, the ban list, at least one numeric identity lock per style that must survive, and a tokens block (durations, springs, stagger) with no adjective-only lines.

steps.title: Decide type and tempo (Phase 1 step 5)
steps.do: Choose one display face, one UI face and the accent, the hook's size and length, and the film's tempo when no track was supplied.
steps.done_when: docs/style_guide.md names both faces, the accent, hook size (>= 1/3 frame height, <= 5 words) and a BPM.

steps.title: Measure the supplied track
steps.do: Run `python3 "<skill>/scripts/motion/beats.py"` on the track so beats, downbeats and hits exist before the storyboard.
steps.done_when: out/beats.json exists with beats, downbeats and hits arrays.

steps.title: Plan a seamless loop
steps.do: Take the whole-cycle mechanics from loop-template.html and plan the seam (last frame equals first, motion through frame 0).
steps.done_when: docs/brief.md states loop length in frames and the seam plan; {slug}.film.html uses loopT.

steps.title: Set up the hand-drawn library
steps.do: Install scripts/hand-drawn once. Study templates/film-template.mjs for its mechanics only (the run() set-up, the frame function, sheet/strip/verify/render) and write film.mjs with this film's own scenes, characters and look from the brief and style guide; apply the all-three-layers override to detail.md.
steps.done_when: film.mjs exists and draws this film's own scenes (none of the template's demo scene remains); docs/style_guide.md states that all three detail layers appear on every surface.

steps.title: Route, formats and film folder (Phase 1 step 6)
steps.do: Use Route A unless the brief names a framework, choose the primary format and its two reflowed siblings and declare the primary in the page (`primary` in window.timeline(), e.g. '16:9', so render.mjs writes it unsuffixed), copy motion.js and take only the seek(t) mechanics from seek-template.html into the film source named for the film.
steps.done_when: {slug}.film.html and motion.js exist; {slug}.film.html defines window.seek, window.timeline (with its primary format), FORMATS and the layout object L; docs/brief.md records route and formats; nothing of the template's scene, palette or type remains; no index.html.

steps.title: Direction funnel wide → 3 → 1
steps.do: Write six one-line directions, develop three with a rendered style frame each, choose one and say why the other two lost.
steps.done_when: docs/direction.md lists six directions, three developed (logline, world, hook, camera language, ending) with style-frame PNG paths that exist, the chosen one, and the reasons.

steps.title: 6 : 3 : 1 hierarchy and colour script
steps.do: Name per shot (or per figure) the quiet 60 %, leading 30 % and found 10 %, then write the colour script, light and texture across the piece with one accent hue.
steps.done_when: docs/colour_script.md has one row per shot/figure with the 60/30/10 split, dominant colour, value, accent placement, key light direction; exactly one accent hue across rows.

steps.title: Caption, states and rest frame
steps.do: For each component, write the caption or readout first (it adds a dimension the figure does not show), then its sequence of states (its keys) and the data-rest frame that carries its point. Name each component file <name>.html for the figure it shows (an ASCII slug of the figure's subject, also when there is only one component). The subject is the idea being explained (binary-search, lru-cache), known now; a mechanism's object is invented later (mech-invent-object) and never names the file, so no step waits on it; the run's slug names the output folder, not the file. Never index.html.
steps.done_when: docs/figure_states.md has, for every component, its file name, caption or readout, states, data-dur and data-rest.

steps.title: Plan the performance
steps.do: Before writing the figure, plan the initialisation order, the pixel budget, the loop that stops at rest and off screen, and where sizes are cached.
steps.done_when: docs/perf_plan.md names, per component, the init order (one heavy figure at a time), the DPR cap 1.5 (1.0 below 480 px), when the loop stops, and where sizes are cached.

steps.title: Study the catalog and the closest example
steps.do: Look up the catalog and read three or four rows near the idea (and its collection page when the idea has one) to see how a concept became an object, and write what each row teaches. When a kit API is unclear, read the source of the example that uses it; build an upstream example only when seeing it run answers a question, and then only that one example under scratch/: copy its folder plus the kit/ and scripts/ folders its imports resolve to into <out>/scratch/anatomy (the command in anatomy-examples-table), never the whole vendored folder and never into the output folder itself. Rows show how a mapping is made: invent your own object, never redraw a published figure, even when the idea has a row.
steps.done_when: docs/catalog_notes.md names the rows studied and what each mapping teaches (and the example sources read); any example built lives under scratch/ and its capture, when taken, is shots/example-<name>.png; docs/mapping.md (step mech-invent-object) names an object of your own, not the published figure's object.

steps.title: Truth first (anatomy step 2)
steps.do: Collect the real numbers and behaviour (sizes, counts, thresholds, curves) and write them as a small pure model module that drives everything.
steps.done_when: docs/truth.md lists each number with its source; model.mjs exports them as a pure module with no DOM access.

steps.title: Invent the object (anatomy step 3)
steps.do: From the idea's verb pick a mechanism family and a nameable object of your own, map part to meaning one to one, and test the mapping (recognisable, plausible, one to one, honest at the edges, failure triggerable, one lit part).
steps.done_when: docs/mapping.md fills CONCEPT, OBJECT, PARTS, NUMBERS, INPUT, FAILURE, TOUR, READOUT, names the catalog rows studied and states that the object is not a published figure's, answers all six tests, and names exactly one lit part.

steps.title: Parts list (anatomy step 4)
steps.do: Write the grouped parts list (base, structure, mechanism, controls, subject) with each part resting on another, avoiding the craft anti-patterns.
steps.done_when: docs/parts.md lists >= 40 parts (40–80 Figure, 80–150 Hero, more for Epic) in the five groups, each with a `on:` host part; exactly one part marked lit. A pin, washer or bolt drawn as its own solid is a part; bolt circles, dots, rings and ribs drawn as a part's details are not.

steps.title: Plan the world and camera (anatomy step 5)
steps.do: Lay out plans in world units ({x,y,w,d,r} and circles), choose azimuth and elevation, and fit with fitProjection.
steps.done_when: view.mjs exists, states azimuth and elevation, and calls fitProjection on the plan points.

steps.title: Round parts and pipe routing
steps.do: Design turned parts by meridians and route pipes and cables port to port along the structure, crossings on straights, collars gapping the pipe, before drawing them.
steps.done_when: geometry.mjs routes come from fillet/tubePieces with real ports at both ends; docs/parts.md lists each route's two mounts.

steps.title: Build geometry once (anatomy step 6)
steps.do: Precompute every static path with the kit builders imported by path from the skill (never copied), looking up each builder's chapter before using it and choosing builders with the kit's known limits in mind (no holes in extrude, hashed placements collide); moving parts are built once at rest and moved with translateAlong. Step command: --value fn=<builder> once per kit builder you know you will call; a builder you reach for later gets a single lookup (lookup.py kit-<builder> --log <out>) before geometry.mjs first calls it.
steps.done_when: geometry.mjs imports the kit from scripts/anatomy/kit/ and, for every kit builder it calls (slabOf, cylinder, extrude, lathe, tubePieces, translateAlong, ...), the matching kit-{fn} topic is in lookups.log before geometry.mjs was created.

steps.title: Painter's order and the audit hook (anatomy step 7)
steps.do: Paint back to front, split wrapping parts into back and front halves, and with pipes, cables or round parts record shapes with A.recorder, set keys with A.settle and end with A.auditOrExit. When parts are added, removed, change slots or rotate, recompute the order from the scene (footprint graph sorted topologically) so the audit checks the order actually drawn.
steps.done_when: build.mjs exists; when docs/parts.md has pipes, cables or round parts it calls A.recorder, A.settle and A.auditOrExit and supports --audit.

steps.title: Turning groups
steps.do: Model the turning subject as groups of convex kit parts with materials, joints flush or tangent, ordered by separating planes, within the 3D performance limits.
steps.done_when: turn.mjs exists using turning(P, { recorder }); `--audit` prints `turn audit passed`.

steps.title: Extract an imported source
steps.do: Extract with scripts/diagram/<format>_extract.py and record what will be redrawn (never converted). Step command: --value format=<drawio|excalidraw|mermaid>.
steps.done_when: docs/fidelity_ledger.md lists every source element and its fate (kept, merged, dropped with reason).

steps.title: Brand skin from the named source
steps.do: Read the printed diagram-overrides first: a brand URL is read with grab.mjs (Chromium through the seeded launchChromium()) or a plain HTTP fetch, never agent-browser, a Playwright MCP or another browser tool, whatever onboarding.md Step 1 says. Then extract and map the brand per onboarding, deciding every choice it would ask about, and save the profile without a confirmation step; never edit the installed style-guide.md.
steps.done_when: docs/skin.md records the source, accent chosen, light/dark defaults and the saved profile slug; style-guide.md is unchanged.

steps.title: Choose a semantic pattern
steps.do: When behaviour, state, enforcement or risk carries the meaning, pick one semantic pattern before the nearest visual type.
steps.done_when: docs/diagram_plan.md names the pattern and the primitives it adds.

steps.title: Pick the type and set the dials
steps.do: Pick the visual type (a semantic pattern first when behaviour carries the meaning), set format, size preset, detail and audience, and check the node budget.
steps.done_when: docs/diagram_plan.md has `Type: <type>` naming one of the type references, `Size: <preset>` naming a size preset (doc-inline by default) or ramp class, the other dials, the node list with count within the type's budget (above 9 nodes it is split) and every decision the source names (a size or scope judgment, a branch) listed as a decision node, and 1–2 focal elements.

steps.title: Lay out on the grid
steps.do: Place every node on the 4 px grid following the chosen type reference's composition and the type ramp of the size preset's class. Step command: --value chosen=<type> (one per type for a split figure) --value size=<preset> (doc-inline, slide-16x9, ...).
steps.done_when: docs/layout.md lists each node's x, y, w, h (all multiples of 4) and the type sizes used; the type-{chosen} and type-ramp-{size} topics are in lookups.log before it was created.

steps.title: The figure card
steps.do: Write each component file with the component mechanics (figure registration, draw function reading colour tokens, visible-only loop, scrubber and play / pause, theme switch, reduced motion, window.seek) and the component contract. Its look comes from its approach's look step (style guide for free creative, anatomy card and tones for a mechanism, diagram tokens for a diagram system), never from the example file's look; no page frame, headline or prose.
steps.done_when: Each component file has theme tokens on :root with both dark guards and an explicit body background, a theme switch, window.seek and data-fig/data-dur/data-rest, an aria-label, its caption or readout; works from 320 px; no external script tags; no page frame or paragraphs.

steps.title: Frame it (anatomy step 8)
steps.do: Put the figure in the card: Fig n top left, title top right, hint bottom left, live readout bottom right, legend and a true caption under the card, no words in the drawing beyond one engraved label. This card and the anatomy tones are the component's look.
steps.done_when: The built file contains a plateHtml card with all four corners filled and the caption under it; the SVG contains at most one text element.

steps.title: Mechanism as a still
steps.do: Deliver the figure at its rest or apart pose as a cut-away or exploded still, built and checked with the same kit.
steps.done_when: {slug}.html shows the rest or apart pose with no live input; docs/audit.txt and shots/lines.png exist for that pose.

steps.title: Markup: tokens, connectors, labels
steps.do: Build the file on the design-system skeleton, not on a picture: the diagram form starts from the template's skeleton (tokens, type, eyebrow and h1 frame); a component takes only the template's tokens and type into its <name>.html and keeps the component contract (no eyebrow, h1 or page frame). The SVG body is written new, its composition from the chosen type reference and docs/layout.md: arrows before boxes with orthogonal elbows, masked labels, the legend as a bottom strip. The diagram form's file is named {slug}.html, a component's is its <name>.html; never index.html.
steps.done_when: The diagram file exists with slug-prefixed <title>/<desc> ids, no diagonal connector paths, every arrow label masked, the legend at the bottom, accent on at most two elements.

steps.title: Traditional Chinese labels
steps.do: Extend the font family with the CJK face and keep the 12 px floor.
steps.done_when: The built file's font stacks include the CJK face and no CJK label is under 12 px.

steps.title: Draw the rest frame first
steps.do: Draw every component's rest frame as a composed still and look at it in both themes before any animation code.
steps.done_when: shots/rest/ holds a light and a dark capture of every component at data-rest; docs/review_log.md has a rest-frame entry per component.

steps.title: Pick a seed blind and promote it
steps.do: Copy each seed's captures to shots/seeds/ under shuffled letters, have a judge in a fresh context score them on the shared card and the form and approach rows that stills can show, write the verdict, then copy the winner into the output folder (not brief, progress or lookups.log), append its lookups.log lines to docs/lookups.log, and continue from the next step on the winner only. Never splice parts of a losing seed into the winner.
steps.done_when: docs/seed_hunt.md has each letter's row scores, overall score and one-line reason, the ranking, the letter-to-seed key, the winner and how the judge ran; the output folder holds the winner's files and docs/lookups.log holds its step records.

steps.title: Make it live (anatomy step 9)
steps.do: Write the idle tour as tourAt(t) with seek(t) writing the pose through the same refs as the live loop (a seek clears the queued future and cancels the idle timer; a fixed-step replay runs to t), and add pointer and keyboard by default, stop offscreen, still under reduced motion.
steps.done_when: live.js exposes seek(t); the figure carries data-dur and data-rest; pointer and keyboard handlers exist; the loop stops at rest; for a film `render.mjs hash` prints DETERMINISTIC.

steps.title: Join the component or film
steps.do: In a component, inline ISO_CSS and kitScript() once per file and follow the component's theme switch; in a film, expose window.seek and window.timeline with shaders drawn from t. Step command: {form} defaults to the brief's Form: line, or pass --value form=<component|film>.
steps.done_when: Component: exactly one kitScript() inline per file and the figure wrapper has class `iso` with data-theme following the root. Film: window.seek and window.timeline exist in {slug}.film.html and no wall-clock or unseeded random is used.

steps.title: Reveal / step / loop motion
steps.do: Copy the controller verbatim from template-motion.html, keeping the static frame complete without JavaScript and under reduced motion.
steps.done_when: The diagram file contains the verbatim controller; with JS off the full diagram renders.

steps.title: Seek overlay
steps.do: Add the seek-overlay script and scrubber so a token travels the real connectors under window.seek(t), then write the static twin with seek_split.py.
steps.done_when: The diagram file defines window.seek; seek_split.py wrote the static twin and its self_check passed.

steps.title: Shader layer (any approach)
steps.do: Whatever the approach, put the effect in a back-SVG / canvas / front-SVG stack with the figure's camera, every uniform on an envelope, a light-theme ink design, and a small shader compiled in parallel with a fallback until ready.
steps.done_when: The shader source (gl.mjs, or the component or film file) is <= ~8 KB after the prelude; compile uses KHR_parallel_shader_compile with a fallback; light-theme blending is premultiplied normal, never screen.

steps.title: Animate and make it answer
steps.do: Animate each component through its states with springs by mass, redrawing only moving parts, and answer pointer and keyboard by default (a still only when the user asked for one).
steps.done_when: shots/states/ holds mid-animation captures of every component; scrubbing to any t reproduces the same frame; reduced motion shows data-rest; pointer and keyboard handlers exist unless the brief records a requested still.

steps.title: Split a long piece before drafting
steps.do: Write ANIMATION_GUIDE.md and the chapter split before any chapter is drafted.
steps.done_when: ANIMATION_GUIDE.md exists with palette, type, camera language, transition vocabulary, exposure, line weights, bans, and the chapter list.

steps.title: Storyboard with timed reads
steps.do: Write the logline, theme and every shot with its ordered reads, event, enter and exit, one read at a time.
steps.done_when: docs/storyboard.md has a logline, a theme, and every shot has at least one timed read, an event, `enter:` and `exit:`.

steps.title: Cinematography plan
steps.do: Plan each shot's size, angle, lens feel, named move with start–end and curve, hold and reason, reusing the direction's two or three moves; look up each named move's chapter before writing its row. Write the move as `Move: <name> …` (one per shot, `Move: none` for a locked-off shot); only those lines name moves, so prose elsewhere in the file is free. Step command: --value move=<name> once per named move (push-in, whip pan, ...; none or static for a locked-off shot).
steps.done_when: docs/camera_plan.md has one row per storyboard shot with every column filled and one `Move: <name>` per shot naming a camera move from camera.md (or none); each named move's camera-{move} topic is in lookups.log before the file was created.

steps.title: A named transition at every seam
steps.do: Choose a transition for every seam (into the first shot, between each pair, out of the last), looking up each chosen transition's chapter. Write each as `Seam: <name> …`; only those lines name transitions. Step command: --value name=<name> once per chosen transition (hard cut, whip pan, push, ...).
steps.done_when: docs/seams.md has shots+1 `Seam: <name>` lines, each naming one transition from transitions.md with its reason; no fade to black between two UI states; each transition-{name} topic is in lookups.log before the file was created.

steps.title: Pacing curve and timing sheet
steps.do: Sketch the intensity curve, check it against the rhythm rules, then write the timing sheet in frames and seconds.
steps.done_when: docs/timing_sheet.md has one row per shot with start/end frames, read frames, move, hold, transition and cue frames, beat numbers; frame 0 is not empty and the hook lands within 2 s; beat frames computed as n×60/BPM.

steps.title: Key list in draft
steps.do: List every key (each read's end state, each shot's enter and exit, each listed state) and start a key card for each.
steps.done_when: docs/keys.md has one card per key with time, read completed, framing, focus and single difference, copy.

steps.title: Keys-only animatic with temp sound
steps.do: Render one still per shot at the timing sheet's times with a temp track or click, and judge whether it reads as a story.
steps.done_when: out/{slug}.animatic.mp4 exists (render.mjs animatic); docs/review_log.md has a Draft-gate entry with every 2-draft checklist item ticked.

steps.title: First and last frames as a pair
steps.do: Render the first and last frames side by side and judge them as a pair: the hook and the payoff/poster.
steps.done_when: out/keys/bookends.png exists; docs/review_log.md has an entry judging the pair; frame 0 already shows the film's most striking image or the question it answers: not empty, not a title card on a flat grey or gradient ground, no decorative particles that belong to no event.

steps.title: Layout of each key
steps.do: Turn each key's shot size, angle and lens feel into numbers: camera rect, depth layers with their p, focus plane.
steps.done_when: docs/key_layout.md has one row per key in docs/keys.md with camera rect, depth layers (p values) and focus plane (or `none`).

steps.title: Pick a film seed blind and promote it
steps.do: The same pick as seed-pick, on each seed's bookends and rendered keys: shuffled letters under shots/seeds/, a judge in a fresh context, the verdict, the winner copied in and its lookups.log lines appended; the shoot, sound and render run on the winner only.
steps.done_when: docs/seed_hunt.md has each letter's row scores, overall score and one-line reason, the ranking, the letter-to-seed key, the winner and how the judge ran; the output folder holds the winner's film folder and keys, and docs/lookups.log holds its step records.

steps.title: KEYS as data, reviewed as stills
steps.do: Write every key as a full scene state in KEYS at its settled time, render one still per key, and critique the sheet before anything moves.
steps.done_when: {slug}.film.html has a KEYS array whose times match docs/keys.md; out/keys/contact.png exists; every key card complete and every key scored >= 8 as a still in docs/review_log.md.

steps.title: Design each interval
steps.do: Write one shot-list line per pair of adjacent keys: what carries, the verb and spring feel by mass, camera, transition, timing, cue.
steps.done_when: docs/shotlist.md has (keys − 1) lines, each with carries, verb (feel), camera, transition, time range, cue.

steps.title: In-betweens from KEYS, camera between framings
steps.do: Compute every animated property as a track over the key times, run the named camera moves between approved framings, then re-render the key stills from the animated build.
steps.done_when: out/keys/settled.png matches the approved key sheet (every key settled at its time); `render.mjs hash` output saved in docs/hash.txt prints DETERMINISTIC.

steps.title: Dailies
steps.do: Review the motion between keys with beats, contact, strips around every fast action, phone and animatic sheets, noting problems by frame number in camera words, and fix at the owning phase.
steps.done_when: out/{slug}.contact.png exists (render.mjs contact); docs/review_log.md has >= 3 dailies rounds, each listing the three worst problems with frame numbers and the fix; every scorecard row >= 8 before post.

steps.title: Execute the seams
steps.do: Draw every transition from docs/seams.md as geometry with beat-derived durations, landing on a beat; write J- and L-cuts as cue times.
steps.done_when: For every Seam line of docs/seams.md a strip around the seam exists in out/seams/; window.timeline() contains the J/L cue entries.

steps.title: Score and sync the sound
steps.do: Generate cues from the picture's timeline at event + 1 frame, build or use the bed, mix with sfx.mjs, and measure on the decoded file.
steps.done_when: out/cues.json and out/mix.wav exist; measurement saved shows integrated loudness about −14 LUFS, true peak < −1 dBTP on the decoded MP4, hits 3–6 dB over the bed, phone band checked.

steps.title: Render the master
steps.do: After Shoot's gate, choose the motion-blur look and run `render.mjs full --html {slug}.film.html --fps 60 --sub 4 --audio out/mix.wav`, with --all when the brief delivers several formats; the master is named for the film.
steps.done_when: out/{slug}.mp4 exists in the primary format (render.mjs prints which primary it used); with --all every other format is written suffixed beside it (out/{slug}-1x1.mp4, out/{slug}-16x9.mp4, or out/{slug}-9x16.mp4 when the primary is not 9:16), and each sibling format named in the brief exists; no final.mp4.

steps.title: Finish: loops, export, poster
steps.do: Export within the platform limits (GIF only when asked), handle the AAC seam for loops, and render the poster from the strongest frame.
steps.done_when: out/{slug}.poster.png exists (render.mjs still --out-file out/{slug}.poster.png at the strongest frame); for a loop out/check/{slug}.loop_check.mp4 exists (checks.sh loop) and the seam check passes; export settings match finishing.md.

steps.title: Review the encoded master
steps.do: Run checks.sh contact|strip|loop|probe on the encoded master and on each sibling (the sheets land in out/check/, named for each file), review muted and with sound, fix the worst defects and repeat until clean.
steps.done_when: docs/export_review.md records probe duration/size/fps/audio stream, sheets every second and at each scene boundary, the final 3-second hold, and a final pass with no open defect.

steps.title: Package
steps.do: Write the folder README with the exact render commands and package the source without secrets or dependency folders (the producer's package for client work).
steps.done_when: README.md exists and contains the exact `render.mjs full …` line; every delivered format opens with the expected size, duration and audio.

steps.title: Author the candidate JSON
steps.do: Pick the map type, read the matching example for shape only, and write the complete candidate led by the main user journey, with meaningful boundaries and labels and automatic routes first. Step command: --value type=<map type>.
steps.done_when: candidate.json validates against its schema, its top-level diagram_type names the map type whose example was looked up, meta.output is `{slug}.map.html` and meta.quality_profile `showcase` (unless standard was asked).

steps.title: Repository evidence
steps.do: Pin the commit and attach sources (path + line) to every asserted node.
steps.done_when: candidate.json records the commit and every asserted node has sources.

steps.title: Viewer features on request
steps.do: Set trace animation, share cards or presentation only when asked.
steps.done_when: candidate.json meta enables only the requested viewer features.

steps.title: Finalize
steps.do: Export ARCHIFY_CHROME, the sandbox opt-out and the update-check switch, run `node "<skill>/scripts/map/bin/archify.mjs" finalize <type> candidate.json {slug}.map.html --quality showcase --json` (add --repo-root for a repository map), save the receipt as docs/finalize.json, and on any non-zero exit repair the connected neighbourhood and rerun the complete command.
steps.done_when: docs/finalize.json is a passing receipt (exit 0, browser check not skipped) and {slug}.map.html exists.

steps.title: Look at the map
steps.do: Always run this review (in /draw it is not optional): run `node "<skill>/scripts/map/bin/archify.mjs" visual-check {slug}.map.html --summary --require-provenance`, which writes the screenshots {slug}.map.visual-check.<WxH>.<theme>.png and the contact sheet {slug}.map.visual-check.html next to the map, then inspect them per the delivery contract and record the visual_review status. Correction rounds continue until the review passes (no two-round cap; the stall rule ends a round that does not change).
steps.done_when: {slug}.map.visual-check.json and its screenshots exist, and docs/review_log.md has the perceptual review entry with its visual_review status and the real number of correction rounds.

steps.title: First version within the first hour
steps.do: As soon as the piece first opens and works in a browser (the diagram or component file, the film source scrubbing in the browser or its first sheet, the map after its first finalize), and at the latest one hour after the run started, send the user its path with one line on what works and what comes next; do not wait for a reply, keep deepening it. This is a milestone in time, not a position in the list: it fires whenever the first openable version exists.
steps.done_when: docs/first_version.md records when it was sent (within 60 minutes of the run's first log line), the path that was sent, what already works and what was still to come.

steps.title: Verify like a critic: the audit to zero (anatomy step 10)
steps.do: Start step 10: run `node build.mjs --audit` and fix every failing check in the geometry, never with a key bias.
steps.done_when: docs/audit.txt ends `audit passed` with every failing line at 0 (and `turn audit passed` from a full run for a 3D figure).

steps.title: Run the line check to zero
steps.do: Run lines.mjs on the built file and its light variant, and in every resting pose via drive.mjs with ["lines"] last in each sequence (it marks the page), and read the ringed PNG.
steps.done_when: shots/lines.png exists and the saved output prints `line ends: 0` for both themes and every resting pose.

steps.title: Captures and 4× close-ups
steps.do: Capture desktop, 390 px, hover, moments across the tour, reduced motion, the apart pose and the no-webgl fallback, and 4× crops over the whole drawing in both themes, with the figure's resume timer stopped before any shot; read every PNG.
steps.done_when: shots/ holds desktop, 390 px, hover, --times, --reduced captures and zoom-*.png crops covering every junction in both themes, assembled and apart.

steps.title: Orbit checks
steps.do: Run turn-check.mjs (fidelity, order, pops, lines, perf) as a full run in the background.
steps.done_when: docs/turn-check.txt shows every turn-check mode passing on a full run.

steps.title: Upstream review checklist
steps.do: Go through every box of the upstream review checklist against the captures and fix what fails, using the common-faults table.
steps.done_when: docs/verify_checklist.md lists every checklist item with pass and the evidence file.

steps.title: Shader transition sheets
steps.do: Make slowed contact sheets across every shader transition and, in light, log ink per frame and crop where ink meets strokes.
steps.done_when: shots/slow-*.png exist for every transition with no pop or colour switch; docs/review_log.md records monotonic ink per frame in light.

steps.title: Machine checks
steps.do: Run self_check.py, any verifier the type reference names, and a browser look with verify-page.mjs --selector svg (Chromium through the seeded launcher from preflight).
steps.done_when: docs/self_check.txt shows self_check.py passing and every named verify-*.py passing; verify-page reports no errors.

steps.title: Taste gate
steps.do: Run the universal anti-patterns and the pre-output checklist on the finished file; any failing row is a fix and a rerun.
steps.done_when: docs/taste_gate.md lists every row with pass; any table-would-do note is carried to the report's 附註.

steps.title: Export PNG or SVG
steps.do: Export the file this run built, named for it, installing a missing tool rather than reporting it.
steps.done_when: The requested {slug}.svg or {slug}.png exists beside {slug}.html.

steps.title: Component lane check
steps.do: Run verify-page.mjs and perf-check.mjs on every component file until both pass, and read the code for the performance rules they cannot measure.
steps.done_when: docs/verify-page.txt shows no console errors and no horizontal scroll at phone width for every component file; docs/perf.txt shows perf-check exit 0 on a D3D11 renderer on Windows for every component file.

steps.title: Score and fix
steps.do: Each round: run the machine checks, open the captures, score the shared card and the form and approach rows, fix the three worst at the owning step. Step command: {form} and {approach} default to the brief's Form: and Approach: lines, or pass --value form=<form> --value approach=<approach>.
steps.done_when: docs/scorecard.md shows every applicable row >= 8, or a row that did not improve over two consecutive rounds is listed under 未做到的 with its last score and the reason; >= 3 rounds for film and component; each round in docs/review_log.md lists three problems with ids or frame numbers.

steps.title: Hand the components to /ui for the page
steps.do: When the request needs a whole page, after every component passed its lane check and the critique loop: write docs/ui_brief.md (readers, order of ideas, each component's path, point and caption, the facts the page may use, and a `Page: <page-name>.html` line naming the page file, distinct from every component file name), then in the same turn invoke /ui through the Skill tool (baransu:ui) with that brief. Do not stop, do not ask the user, no subagent by default. /ui designs the page and embeds the components; run verify-page.mjs and perf-check.mjs on the page too.
steps.done_when: docs/ui_brief.md lists every component file (each exists), the request summary and a `Page:` line; the page it names, written by /ui, exists, differs from every component file and embeds every component; docs/verify-page.txt and docs/perf.txt have a section for the page.

steps.title: Lookup ledger check
steps.do: Run `python3 "<skill>/scripts/ledger-check.py" "<project>/.claude/draw/<slug>"` against references/steps.json and docs/lookups.log.
steps.done_when: ledger-check.py exits 0.

steps.title: Deliver with the completion report
steps.do: Send the completion report in the SKILL.md format: the files (named for what they show), the form and approach, which path ran (one piece, or components + /ui page), the checks that ran and their results, the scores and rounds, the ledger-check result, 未做到的 with reasons, and the statement that no question was put to the user (unless a real asset or fact was missing).
steps.done_when: The report follows SKILL.md § Completion report; every check it names ran in this session and its result is quoted from the actual output.
